facts.raw_span: skin fragility since early infancy
Symptoms improved in winter and worsened in summer
Mild xerosis with superficial skin erosions
Erythematous residual macules from previous erosions
Some lesions had unusual linear geographic contour
Lesions predominantly located at areas of friction
No history of blistering
Serological markers for celiac disease were negative
Complete separation of the stratum corneum
Clean split just above the stratum granulosum
2 heterozygous mutations in exon 2 of the CDSN gene
Normal results for: Collagen IV and VII, α6 and β4 integrines, Laminine-332

concepts.why: The patient's skin fragility since early infancy, mild xerosis with superficial skin erosions, and complete separation of the stratum corneum are consistent with peeling skin syndrome, which is also supported by the 2 heterozygous mutations in exon 2 of the CDSN gene.
The patient's symptoms improving in winter and worsening in summer, and lesions predominantly located at areas of friction, are consistent with keratosis pilaris.
The patient's mild xerosis with superficial skin erosions and erythematous residual macules from previous erosions are consistent with ichthyosis.
The patient's lesions with unusual linear geographic contour and lesions predominantly located at areas of friction are consistent with atopic dermatitis.
The patient's symptoms improving in winter and worsening in summer, and lesions predominantly located at areas of friction, are consistent with pityriasis rubra pilaris.
The patient's complete separation of the stratum corneum and clean split just above the stratum granulosum are consistent with exfoliative dermatitis.
The patient's 2 heterozygous mutations in exon 2 of the CDSN gene are consistent with genetic epidermolysis bullosa.
The patient's complete separation of the stratum corneum and normal results for collagen IV and VII, α6 and β4 integrines, and laminine-332 are consistent with acquired epidermolysis bullosa.
The patient's mild xerosis with superficial skin erosions and 2 heterozygous mutations in exon 2 of the CDSN gene are consistent with inherited ichthyosis.
The patient's symptoms improving in winter and worsening in summer, and lesions predominantly located at areas of friction, are consistent with erythrokeratodermia.

The patient's symptoms of skin fragility, superficial skin erosions, and peeling skin, combined with negative serological markers for celiac disease and normal immunofluorescence mapping results, are consistent with peeling skin syndrome type B.

rationales.F01: Skin fragility since early infancy suggests a genetic condition, which is more consistent with peeling skin syndrome.
rationales.F02: Seasonal variation in symptoms could be related to environmental factors, but it is not specific to any condition.
rationales.F05: Unusual linear geographic contour of lesions is a distinctive feature of peeling skin syndrome.
rationales.F07: Absence of blistering rules out genetic epidermolysis bullosa and acquired epidermolysis bullosa.
rationales.F09: Complete separation of the stratum corneum is a characteristic histopathological feature of peeling skin syndrome.
rationales.F10: Clean split just above the stratum granulosum is a characteristic histopathological feature of peeling skin syndrome.
rationales.F11: Heterozygous mutations in the CDSN gene are associated with peeling skin syndrome.
